_comment: SmartCuff GUI update manifest. Fetched by the installed GUI over plain
public HTTPS -- there is deliberately NO credential in the client. See
README.md for why an embedded token was rejected.
This file is the ONLY thing the updater needs to read. Keep it small and
keep it valid JSON: a malformed manifest must fail soft in the client, but
there is no reason to rely on that.
The installer is a GitHub Release asset rather than a repository blob.
Keep installer_url version-specific: an existing manifest must always
resolve to the exact immutable bytes whose size and SHA-256 it declares.
notes:
Smart Cuff v3.1.353 (Default) with firmware rev27v-followup-338.

Constant-pressure settling is now bounded: after the refill pump stops, Regular, High Max and Smart Const start their sealed, pump-off 30-second hold within 9.5 seconds. Pressure above the hold band is lowered by short measured valve bleeds and pressure below it is raised by short measured pump top-ups. If the original settling check has not passed by 9.5 seconds, the hold starts anyway and Events shows a REFILL_SETTLE_DEADLINE warning. The previous 60-second stop-and-vent is removed. Bench evidence on Device D (wrist cuff on syringe, simulator pulses on and off): 12 of 12 holds started 1.3-9.5 seconds after pump-off with no deadline flags; every 2.5-second hold error was within 2 mmHg. Large cuffs have not yet been measured with this firmware.

GUI: Control and SysID diagnostics are collapsible; SysID shows probe checks and response stability in a compact table and distinguishes push/save status from repeatability; plot toolbars wrap on narrow windows; plotting does less work while keeping peaks and measurement statistics on original samples; four offline correctness fixes.

The update flashes the bundled firmware through the protected uploader, which snapshots and restores each controller's calibration and tuning.
_channel_note: stable is the only channel today. If a test channel is ever added, publish
a second manifest (version-beta.json) rather than adding branching logic to
the client -- the client stays a dumb fetch-and-compare.
